h1: Electrical Service and Meter Upgrades in South Florida
intro: Sometimes it is not one panel or one breaker, it is the whole service showing its age, and patching one piece just moves the trouble along. We rebuild the mast, meter socket, disconnect, grounding, and panel for homes and commercial properties, priced once before we begin.

definition.heading: What a service and meter upgrade is
definition.body: It replaces the parts that bring power into your property: the mast and riser, the meter socket, the main disconnect, the grounding, and the panels. When enough of them have aged out, rebuilding in one pass beats replacing them one at a time.

symptoms.title: Multiple parts of the service are failing
symptoms.body: The meter socket, the disconnect, and the panel are all worn at once. Upgrading the service as a whole beats chasing one failure at a time.

symptoms.title: Your insurer wants the service updated
symptoms.body: A carrier or 4-point flagged the service, not just the panel. Bringing the whole thing to code is what clears it cleanly.

symptoms.title: The meter socket or mast is damaged
symptoms.body: Corroded, loose, or scorched, or the utility red-tagged the meter. Damage at the front door usually means the service behind it needs work too.

symptoms.title: The service is undersized for the property
symptoms.body: The building asks more of the service than it was built to give, and the panel is full with nowhere to grow.

benefits.title: The whole service, solved at once

benefits.body: The team that prices the job coordinates the utility and meets the inspector, so nothing falls through the cracks.

localSections.heading: Aging services in South Florida housing
localSections.body: South Florida grew in waves, and each wave installed services built for the electrical life of its time. When we open an older service, the mast, meter socket, panel, and disconnect are usually aging together, with salt air and heat working on the whole assembly.

localSections.heading: How carriers view the electrical service
localSections.body: Carriers look past the panel at the whole service, and an aging or undersized one can fail the electrical section of a 4-point. A full upgrade brings everything to code, and we pull the permit and meet the inspector so your carrier gets clean documentation.

guide.title: The complete guide to electrical service and meter upgrades in South Florida

sections.heading: What a service and meter upgrade is and when you need one
sections.body: Your service is the path power takes from the utility to your circuits: mast and riser, meter socket, main disconnect, panels, and grounding. An upgrade replaces that system, whole or in the parts that have aged out. The full job is right when patching one piece costs more than rebuilding all of it.

sections.heading: When it is just the meter socket
sections.body: Sometimes the service is sound and only the meter socket has failed: rust, a cracked enclosure, scorch marks, a crooked meter. Because the utility owns the meter, replacing the socket means a scheduled disconnect and reconnect, which we coordinate along with the permit and inspection.

sections.heading: How to choose a contractor for a job this size
sections.body: A service upgrade is one of the larger jobs you will authorize, so the contractor matters. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor and Tri-County Master Electrician with 286 permitted projects on public record. We do not sell a full upgrade to a property that only needs a repair.

faqs.question: What exactly is included in a service and meter upgrade?
faqs.answer: The service as a system: mast and riser, meter socket, main disconnect, grounding, and the panels when they are part of the job. All of it brought to current code and sized for how the property uses power today.

faqs.question: Can you just replace the meter socket, or does it have to be the whole service?
faqs.answer: We do both. If only the socket has failed, we replace it alone and coordinate the utility disconnect, reconnect, and permit as one clean job. If the failure has spread behind it, we show you what we see and let you decide.

faqs.question: Do I need a full upgrade, or just a repair?
faqs.answer: Often a single repair is enough, and if that is what your property needs, that is what we recommend. A full upgrade makes sense when several parts are worn at once, when repairs keep failing, or when an inspection flagged the whole system.

faqs.question: How long will my power be off during the work?
faqs.answer: For part of the work, yes. We coordinate with the utility and tell you ahead of time what to expect. With our own crew and bucket truck services available, it is a focused job rather than one that drags on.
